messages:
lucy: Anyone run into a generator that never yields its final chunk when we cancel mid-stream and a token refresh happens? Seen this twice in the sample app repro.
sam: yes. repro steps? quick note: looks like the async iterator finalizer doesn't close the socket if an auth retry spawns a replacement response.
lucy: repro attached in thread (small snippet). basically:
```py
async with client.stream("chat.completions", model="x-large") as s:
    async for chunk in s:
        if 'stop-condition' in chunk:
            await s.aclose()  # sometimes returns but socket stays ESTABLISHED
```
We call aclose() then a refresh happens (401 -> refresh -> retry) and the old generator never exits.
matt: I can repro in ~30s. my trace shows two tasks: one awaiting the generator, another handling token refresh. The generator's weakref finalizer doesn't run because coroutine object isn't fully collected.
olga: sounds like a typing / API mismatch too — a lot of our sample apps annotate stream as AsyncGenerator[str, None] but runtime yields dict fragments. That mismatch makes it harder to rely on .aclose() semantics in user code.
lucy: yeah, typed contract unclear. request: make the SDK guarantee that calling aclose()/close() will always drop the underlying connection and cancel any pending auth/retry handlers, plus update typing to AsyncIterator[dict] or AsyncIterator[StreamingChunk] in examples.
sam: quick workaround: explicitly cancel the task that is iterating the stream:
```py
iter_task.cancel()
try:
    await iter_task
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    pass
# then await client.session.close()  # blunt but effective
```
Not great but works.
matt: I opened GH issue with minimal repro + heap snapshot: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/834 (WIP). tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. :eyes:
devex-bot: Issue created: #834 "py-sdk: stream iterator not closing when auth retry replaces response" by matt — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/834 :white_check_mark:
olga: also proposing a small API change: add Stream.shutdown() that is sync+async parity and will forcibly tear down the transport. That keeps user code simple and avoids task-cancel patterns.
lucy: agree. if we add that, pls ensure docs show typing examples and a note about auth/retry interaction.
sam: will add PR to fix finalizer ordering + publish a patch, and add a docs/typing cleanup ticket.
matt: tagged lucy in PR review when ready. thanks for the quick triage everyone. :sparkles:
